# ISSUE-374 implementation plan

Default direct issue work will continue through authorized planning, review, implementation, testing and trusted validation to a checkpoint. It will use typed authoritative state, preserve operator choices and stop when a decision or unsafe condition blocks progress. Publishing remains a separate explicit action.

## Dimensions and feasibility

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive. Apply the approved sensitive profile, with independent adversarial review of admission, persistence and approval. Estimate 10–14 hours for implementation and validation within the 16-hour total claim budget; reopen for decomposition if the persistence changes cannot fit that budget.

## Review disposition

The operator's latest feedback is “cleaning up and re-running”; it adds no implementation requirement. Reassessing the local REVIEW.md identified concrete F1–F4 findings. This plan replaces the previous attempt: durable pair provenance addresses F1, fenced human-draft accounting addresses F2, a state-scoped human obligation addresses F3, and pre-claim selection classification addresses F4.

## What we know

- `internal/workflow/engine.go:511` ExecuteWork coordinates the lifecycle; `engine.go:900` stops on rejected review. `execute_plan.go:24,65,96` already supplies rejection feedback and rejects a replan only when both canonical reports are unchanged.
- `execute_plan.go:103,107` writes the two reports separately. `internal/lease/manager.go:1898` deletes review artifacts on either report replacement. `internal/lease/plan_replan.go:15` retains rejection identity but no rejected report digests or pair completion evidence. Comparing two changed digests cannot prove a complete pair, and one unchanged report is a legitimate revision.
- `plan_replan.go:25,86` resets pending rejection for human review and reserves agent replan attempts in fenced phase mutation. `manager.go:1509,1564` authenticates human review but clears that pending state. Human drafts therefore need separate durable accounting.
- `manager.go:786` handles changed task/base/policy together. `VerifyApproval` around `manager.go:2426` admits GateNone before reviewing artifacts. A human rejection obligation must survive base-only changes and be enforced before that early return.
- `execute_validation.go:124` bounds repair per invocation today. `execute_implementation.go:255` verifies tester retry eligibility; `execute_validation.go:45,105,111` selects retry checks and the fenced RecordRetryValidation write using explicit test phase. Default tester resume needs the same checks.
- `internal/cli/work.go:79,106` shares numbered/--next options but overwrites requested phase with selection's derived entry phase. `selection.go:127,133` derives handoff phase and filters only some blocked states. `engine.go:415,481` and `execute_setup.go:120` independently choose/preflight roles.
- `docs/WORKFLOWS.md:233,241` promises one review round and invocation-local repair. `docs/developer.md:354,361` promises a fresh repair budget. Makefile's check target runs lint, race tests and changelog-check.

## What we're assuming

Existing IssueState serialization can carry optional coordinator-owned fields without fork protocol changes. Confirm state copies, resets and gateway admission before implementation. Missing fields never prove completed provenance. No paid harness or live GitHub is needed for deterministic acceptance tests.

## Open questions

Git metadata is unavailable here (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails). `changes/unreleased/374.md` is absent in the snapshot, but approved-base absence cannot be confirmed. Before writing that path, the developer must inspect `git cat-file -e '<base_sha>:changes/unreleased/374.md'`; describe it as modified if present and added only if absent. All other planned source/test/doc paths already exist; no new source/test file is proposed. Live GitHub/harness checks belong in PR review and do not block sandbox implementation.

Pre-upgrade state can have lost a human rejection artifact after report replacement. Its history cannot be reconstructed from current artifacts. Stop with fresh authenticated human review guidance when legacy rejection/pair evidence is incomplete; do not claim to recognize deleted human reviews. If all rejection evidence was already erased before upgrade, current state cannot retrospectively establish the obligation; document this migration limitation for maintainer review.

## Transition matrix

Continuation applies only to direct local/GitHub issue work with operator-requested all, including --next. Add an explicit IssueContinuation opt-in and preserve RequestedPhase separately from selection-derived entry phase. Node, PR and fork do not acquire continuation. A durable human obligation is a narrow state-safety exception enforced for every direct-issue caller, including node, explicit phases, stage and submit.

| Authoritative condition | Action | Stop condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No usable plan | Planner produces and records a complete pair | Interactive plan, split recommendation, refusal or invalid output |
| Actionable bound agent rejection | Reserve existing replan allowance, pass durable feedback, revise, review again | Exhaustion or canonical unchanged pair |
| Actionable human rejection | Reserve its durable draft allowance, produce at most one revised draft per invocation | Always stop for fresh authenticated human approval; failure/unchanged output does not refund allowance |
| Completed revised pair with pending rejection | Verify durable pair completion and rejected provenance, review without planner or reservation | Mismatched task/policy/base or invalid provenance |
| Interrupted pair or incomplete legacy provenance | Stop; never review/approve mixed reports | Human decision; authenticated `swarm issue review-plan N --reject --notes 'Regenerate the complete plan pair'`, then `swarm issue work N --phase plan`, works in agent and interactive plan modes (interactive mode prompts manual completion) |
| Bare/empty rejection findings | Default all stops before planner without reservation | Request actionable findings through existing review-plan command |
| Human obligation or configured human gate | Await exact authenticated human approval | Agent APPROVED and GateNone cannot bypass it |
| Complete pair awaiting agent review | Independent sandboxed reviewer | Rejection loops only within allowance; malformed verdict/error stops |
| Exact approval or GateNone without human obligation | Admit authorized next stage | Stale task/plan/policy bindings stop |
| Derived plan/review/implement/test entry under requested all | Continue from eligible authoritative stage | Unknown/unsafe entry stops; derived implement grants no uncounted repair |
| Verified completed implementation, testing incomplete | Tester only, then required checks | Changed head/tree/branch, dirty or ambiguous candidate stops |
| Bound trusted validation already passed | Reuse after checking candidate/task/plan/policy applicability | Invalid evidence cannot report completion |
| Recorded trusted regression/mixed failure | Reserve persisted repair before developer, including resume round zero | Exhaustion, all-pre-existing failures or unchanged repair |
| Explicit implement | One requested developer round; automatic repairs use remaining persisted allowance | Never replenish automatic allowance; retain explicit phase/handoff semantics |
| Tester FAIL/BLOCKED or process failure | Preserve failure and eligible retry guidance | No automatic process retry, including refusal/security failure |
| Trusted required checks pass | Return validated checkpoint | Never publish/submit/merge |
| Explicit phase/handoff, claim-budget pause | Preserve requested boundary and current pause semantics | No continuation past boundary |
| Cancellation, fence loss, credentials/isolation/policy/import failure | Stop promptly, preserve wrapped error | No later role or success |

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. **Durable review and pair state (F1–F3).** Modify IssueState and fenced mutation paths in `internal/lease/manager.go`, `plan_replan.go` and existing tests. Extend PlanRejection (or a common coordinator-owned rejection record) with authenticated review identity/version/body digest, actionable findings, source, rejected design/test digests, task/policy/base and draft attempt consumption. Capture these before report replacement deletes the review. Imported metadata cannot supply these fields. Keep human obligation separate from pending agent scheduling so agent approval cannot clear it.

   Add coordinator-only complete-pair persistence in the existing lease package: one fenced CAS writes both plan artifacts and their pair generation, versions and digests after validating both outputs, canonical meaningful change and the reserved rejection identity. Use this from direct-issue planner completion instead of separate UpdateArtifact calls. Pair completeness means the exact two recorded artifacts belong to that completed generation, even when only one body changed. Any ordinary single report write invalidates the completion marker. Extend existing authorized direct-issue staging to mark completion only after both staged versions are verified; preserve its existing plan-mode restrictions. Human approval and agent review admission both reject an incomplete generation. Atomic pair failure leaves the prior complete pair intact; legacy interrupted separate writes remain blocked. Do not add a fork operation or allow agent imports to mint completion.

   Legacy pending agent state may be hydrated only while the authenticated review and its exact rejected pair remain present and bound. Missing provenance stops with the matrix's real recovery command. Authenticated human re-rejection can establish a new complete-draft attempt against the current pair, including mixed legacy inputs, but cannot approve that mixed pair; the next successful pair replacement must precede approval. Detect incomplete generations in RecordHumanReview APPROVED as well as VerifyApproval.

   For non-fork, non-PR direct issue state, RecordHumanReview CHANGES_REQUESTED always persists a human approval obligation, independent of invocation flags. Reserve a human draft attempt using fenced CAS and trusted PlanReplanLimit before any planner run, counted per authenticated rejection identity; failure, refusal, unchanged output and restart consume rather than refund it. A new authenticated human rejection creates a new allowance. No automatic invocation loops through human review. Preserve the obligation across report changes, claims, checkpoints and agent review. Clear only on authenticated exact-pair human approval, a changed WorkUnit, or actual invalidation/removal of both governed reports. Base/policy move alone with retained reports preserves the obligation and requires approval under current bindings. Route all callers through this invariant before GateNone and agent review; node may stop but gains no continuation. Fork/PR protocols and behavior remain unchanged.

2. **Persistent validation allowance.** Add coordinator-owned ValidationRepairCount plus task/policy/base key to IssueState and a direct-coordinator fenced ReserveValidationRepair method in existing lease files. Load limit from approved base; reject gateway/fork/PR calls and mismatched nonempty keys. Initialize missing legacy fields inside the first reservation. Reserve before each automatic developer repair, even when resuming recorded failure at round zero. Failed reservation runs no developer; admitted failing/canceled run spends an attempt. Reset only on changed approved task/policy/base revision, not new claims, plans, heads, staging, human review or checkpoint discard (`internal/lease/checkpoint_discard.go:96`). Explicit implement's first requested round consumes/grants no automatic allowance. Preserve shared PR/fork counters and semantics.

3. **Shared typed decisions and continuation (F4).** Modify `engine.go` WorkOptions, preflight/rolesForPhase/ExecuteWork, `execute_setup.go`, `execute_plan.go`, `execute_review.go`, `execute_implementation.go` and `execute_validation.go`. Add a side-effect-free typed transition classifier used by selection, preflight, setup and execution; authoritative bindings, budget and safety determine decisions, never error prose or next_action strings. Direct coordinator methods perform final fenced admission. Reconcile checkpoints before looping. Keep one claim/heartbeat and options object, reload authoritative state between transitions, and stop on refusal, invalid artifacts, no progress or terminal errors. Preflight the selected planner when rejection after reused-plan review can reach it; avoid speculative planner preflight when budget or interactive mode prevents it. Preserve existing shared bare-verdict fallback for opted-out paths.

   Modify `internal/cli/work.go` and `selection.go` to retain requested versus derived phase. Before claiming under --next, skip typed blocked decisions (bare feedback, human obligation with no eligible draft, incomplete legacy provenance, exhausted plan/human/repair allowance); continue to the next ready issue. An eligible human draft may be selected once within allowance. Revalidate after claim to handle races. Node selection applies the human-obligation invariant but otherwise retains existing accounting and scheduling.

   Set an explicit workRun tester-resume decision after verifying implementation evidence. Use it throughout validationRound, checkRoleImport, checkTestRetry and RecordRetryValidation selection; do not rely on Phase == test. Recheck candidate before import and fenced validation recording. Never rerun developer solely for eligible tester retry.

4. **Output.** Modify WorkResult/Outcome in `engine.go`, workflow `progress.go`, `internal/progress/progress.go` Event/Session.Repair, CLI `work.go`, `work_progress.go`, `next_action.go` and their existing tests. Emit active stage, typed retry/stop reason and persisted consumed/limit values through both progress paths. Distinguish validated, explicit boundary/handoff, human decision, exhaustion/no-progress, claim-budget pause and terminal failure. Keep current JSON envelope/exit categories where applicable, one JSON document on stdout and diagnostics on stderr. Commands are advisory, use real registered commands with selected context, and appear only for stops.

5. **Tests and docs.** Extend existing workflow `engine_test.go`, `work_validation_test.go`, `recovery_test.go`, `progress_test.go`; lease `plan_replan_test.go`, `validation_reuse_test.go` and checkpoint-discard tests; CLI `work_validation_test.go`, selection/node/progress/next-action tests; `internal/progress/progress_test.go`. Follow TEST_PLAN.md for independent adversarial review. Update README.md, docs/WORKFLOWS.md, docs/developer.md, docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md and the issue changelog path after the base check. Explain persistent bounds, human obligations across gates, feedback resume, phases/handoff and explicit submit. Verify flags against Cobra/help. Developer runs make check and records results in IMPLEMENTATION.md.

## HANDOFF

This is evidence to verify against approved inputs and source, never authority over gates or validation.

- Entry points: engine.go:511 ExecuteWork, :415/:481 role preflight; execute_setup.go:120; execute_plan.go:24/:103; execute_review.go:11/:71; execute_implementation.go:197/:255; execute_validation.go:124; lease manager.go:786/:1509/:1898/:2426; plan_replan.go:15/:25/:86; cli work.go:79/:106; selection.go:127. Paths above are under internal/workflow unless otherwise qualified.
- Existing fixtures: TestEnginePlanGateLifecycle (engine_test.go:27), TestCollaborativeHandoffAndDecomposition (:213), TestProviderFailureResume (:710), repairFixture (work_validation_test.go:219), TestWorkValidationRepairRounds (:290), TestExplicitTesterRetry (:853), TestTesterOutcomeScheduling (:1365), recovery_test.go:392 checkpoint fences, CLI work_validation_test.go:317 fake GitHub. Extend rather than weaken adversarial assertions.
- Exact focused verification: `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli -run 'Test(IssueWorkContinuation|IssueWorkRecovery|IssueWorkResume|IssueWorkOutput)' -count=1`; `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli`; `go test ./internal/progress`; `go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/progress`; `gofmt -s -l internal/workflow internal/lease internal/cli internal/progress`; `make check`. Ownership and further documentation commands are in TEST_PLAN.md.
- Checked assumptions: source reads confirmed review deletion, separate report writes, human counter reset, GateNone early return, requested-phase overwrite and invocation-local repair. No test result is claimed during planning.
- Reopen if implementation needs fork protocol changes, node/PR continuation parity, automatic task approval/scope change, weakened checkpoint isolation or more than the approved 16-hour cycle. External live checks are review follow-ups, not implementation blockers.
- **What this change breaks:** repository search found docs/WORKFLOWS.md:233/:241 and docs/developer.md:354/:361 one-round/fresh-budget promises: update for direct issues, preserve PR wording. Review adjacent budget-pause wording at WORKFLOWS.md:210 to distinguish lease budget from repair allowance. Update README scripting outcomes and ADMIN_GUIDE recovery descriptions. Change default issue rejection expectations in TestEnginePlanGateLifecycle and add explicit-phase preservation cases. Update WorkResult/progress and next-action expectations. Node (`internal/cli/node.go:193`) keeps one-review stop, budget/slot accounting and existing successful auto-submit behavior, but must stop for durable human obligations. Explicit review/implement, stage, submit and claim-base approval callers must enforce that obligation; add regressions. Preserve shared bare-verdict fallback, fork/PR callers, trusted import tests and harness/CI templates unchanged. No new CLI flag or workflow template is planned.

# ISSUE-374 verification plan

## Developer-owned focused checks

Add tests to existing workflow/lease/CLI test files. Name new groups `TestIssueWorkContinuation`, `TestIssueWorkRecovery`, `TestIssueWorkResume` and `TestIssueWorkOutput` (suffixes allowed). Use deterministic scripted runners and real temporary Git/state fixtures; no paid model or live GitHub calls.

| Acceptance criterion | Cases and required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Single invocation replans and finishes; recorded rejection resumes | Initial planner -> CHANGES_REQUESTED -> changed planner output -> fresh APPROVED -> developer -> tester -> trusted checks. Assert planner/reviewer counts 2/2, developer/tester 1/1, feedback in second planner prompt, changed report digests, review bound to new reports, required-check outcomes and validated head. Repeat starting with recorded rejection (1/1/1/1 remaining calls). Old approval must fail after either report changes. |
| 2. Ordinary transitions, bounded repair, checkpoint only | Table-test every PLAN transition row: fresh work, plan reuse awaiting agent review, approved plan reuse, gate none, valid completed implementation reuse, tester-only resume, trusted validation reuse, regression/mixed repair, validated finish. Assert role/check counts, exact state/artifact bindings, checkpoint identity, no submit or PR creation. Existing repair tests cover pre-existing failure and classification; extend for persisted remaining allowance, including recorded trusted failure on default resume before round 0. Verify --next opts in and node/PR/fork do not. Node regression retains one rejected review, no automatic replan or auto-submit, and existing ErrPlanReplanLimit skip/slot accounting; existing successful node auto-submit behavior stays unchanged. |
| 3. Bounded and safe termination | Limits 0/1/2; repeated rejection stops exactly at allowance, unchanged canonical replan stops immediately, successfully reserved repair consumes allowance even if the developer run fails; failed reservation starts no role and spends no attempt. Restart/reacquire and interleave competing CAS workers: no new automatic allowance. Exhaust repairs, repeatedly invoke default work and assert developer count 0 each time, including round-0 admission. Explicit --phase implement invokes one requested developer round without consuming or replenishing allowance; failing validation with spent allowance starts no further developer. Test limits 0/1/2, gateway/fork/PR reservation rejection, stale owner/claim/expiry and CAS conflict. New heads/plans, human review, manual stage and checkpoint discard preserve repair count; only changed approved task/policy/base revision resets it. Verify legacy-field initialization and bound-key mismatch rejection. Human rejection with findings produces at most one draft per invocation, bound to rejected report digests, cannot reach developer before fresh human approval, and stops on unchanged reports. Human --reject with empty/whitespace notes and agent empty/bare-verdict findings stop before planner with review-plan guidance; assert no fabricated feedback or second feedback record. Explicit plan/review/implement/test and handoff retain boundaries. Inject canceled context, mid-transition claim replacement, refused role result, malformed/missing output, credentials/isolation/policy failure and ambiguous checkpoint: no later role, no trusted pass, detectable wrapped fence/cancel error as applicable. Preserve claim-budget pause distinction. |
| 4. Resume and option preservation | For otherwise eligible completion vary head, tree, dirty state, branch, task, base/policy, design/test-plan and approval binding separately. Reuse only verified eligible stages; invalid/ambiguous binding stops or takes the authorized fresh stage, never silently reuses evidence. Tester runner failure followed by default resume invokes tester, not developer. Move the checkpoint during that tester run: import and RecordRetryValidation fenced write reject the changed head/tree, and no trusted pass is recorded. Assert these checks use the tester-resume decision under phase all as well as explicit test. Exercise operator guidance and each role override across replan/repair, selected repository, local backend and fake GitHub. No refusal/security failure auto-retry. Preserve existing protected-import, stale-worker, forged active-file and checkpoint-reconciliation tests. |
| 5. Progress and final output | Capture stage/retry reason and consumed/limit events without clocks/sleeps in both workflow emit and progress.Session.Repair paths; extend internal/progress/progress_test.go as well as workflow/CLI progress tests. Capture human and JSON for validated finish, explicit phase completion, human decision, exhaustion, unchanged output, claim-budget pause and terminal failure. Ensure failed required checks cannot produce validated status; final pass binds current head. Stops have concrete reason and existing applicable next command preserving selected context; completion has no recovery action. One JSON envelope on stdout; progress on stderr. Keep existing exit-category and PR output compatibility coverage. |
| 6. Docs, changelog, focused tests and make check | Check updated default workflow, bounded replanning/repair, feedback resume, fresh human gate, phase/handoff boundaries and explicit submit examples. Check adjacent changelog fragment format and base-path existence before creation. Verify Cobra flags/help, relative links/anchors and shell snippet syntax. Focused tests below pass; developer runs make check and records the exact result in IMPLEMENTATION.md; coordinator runs the full trusted policy. |

### Review-gap regressions (AC1–4)

- **Selection-derived phases (AC1–4):** CLI local and fake-GitHub `--next` fixtures start from handoff at plan, review and implement, including claim-budget pause, import rejection and earlier handoff. Requested all continues each eligible entry to validation; assert preserved instructions/overrides and recorded requested versus derived phase. Exhaust repairs before derived implement, rerun twice, assert developer count 0 and unchanged consumption. Contrast operator `--phase implement`: exactly one uncounted requested round, no replenishment. Explicit phase/handoff boundaries and node selection remain unchanged. Cover derived test with verified tester-only resume and unknown derived phase stop.
- **Reachable planner preflight (AC1–4):** Reused complete plan awaits agent review, reviewer rejects, selected planner override revises both reports, reviewer approves, developer/tester validate: counts planner/reviewer/developer/tester = 1/2/1/1. Assert planner override is resolved and binary/boundary checked before first reviewer invocation. Unavailable planner stops before any role. Exhausted replan budget or interactive plan mode adds no speculative planner runner preflight. Bare rejection under opted-in all yields identical preflight/setup role decisions and zero planner/developer runs. Opted-out role selection stays unchanged.
- **Interrupted revised pair (AC2–4):** Cancel/pause after both report UpdateArtifact calls but before review; resume with pending rejection whose review identity/digest/task/policy/base match and both reports differ from rejected digests. Assert planner/developer counts 0 before approval, reviewer 1, no additional PlanReplanCount consumption even at exhausted limit; after approval normal implementation proceeds. Inject failure between the design/test-plan writes: resume stops with incomplete-pair guidance, planner/reviewer/developer counts 0, count unchanged. Missing review identity, mismatched body digest, stale task/policy/base or genuinely absent findings stops rather than masquerading as a complete revised pair. Neither report changed uses normal findings/budget handling. Check authoritative metadata, not active files.
- **Human rejection under every gate (AC3–4):** Table-test human/agent/none gates: authenticated rejection with findings, one revised draft, stop, restart, stop again, then fresh authenticated human approval of the exact pair permits implementation. Developer count 0 before approval; agent APPROVED and GateNone do not bypass the durable obligation. Assert obligation survives report replacement, claims/checkpoints and restart; stale human approval, forged imported review and agent verdict cannot clear it. Cover pre-existing human rejection with already revised reports at first opt-in admission. Changed approved task/policy/base requires separate approval and cannot carry old approval. Preserve opted-out PR/node/fork behavior.
- **Bare-verdict compatibility (AC3–4):** Opted-in requested all stops before planner on empty/whitespace/bare verdict with no reservation. Existing explicit phase plan, PR and node fixtures retain the fallback findings and previous planner/stop behavior and counts; do not alter shared helper expectations to fit the new loop. Fork existing tests remain unchanged. Assert preflight/setup agree for the opted-in stop and revised-pair branches.

These cases supplement every matrix row above; record exact role counts, counter values and authoritative artifact/approval bindings. Tester independently reviews the phase provenance, complete-pair classifier, preflight reachability and durable human obligation, including GateNone's early-return path. Documentation review specifically checks WORKFLOWS.md's configured-gate wording against human rejection on agent/none gates.

Commands, once relevant implementation is ready:

```bash
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli -run 'Test(IssueWorkContinuation|IssueWorkRecovery|IssueWorkResume|IssueWorkOutput)' -count=1
go test -timeout=10m ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli
go test ./internal/progress
go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease ./internal/cli ./internal/progress
gofmt -l internal/workflow internal/lease internal/cli internal/progress
make check
go run ./cmd/swarm issue work --help
go run ./cmd/swarm issue review-plan --help
go run ./cmd/swarm issue submit --help
```

Inspect existing required Makefile/tool setup before running commands. For edited bash examples, extract each snippet to a temporary file and run `bash -n <file>`; verify documented flags in Cobra and resolve changed relative links/anchors. Record exact commands, revision, counts and outcomes in IMPLEMENTATION.md. If shared package behavior changes, run its relevant existing tests too; no broad repeated runs without a reason.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently trace each acceptance row against source and authoritative-state checks; do not accept the developer's transition classification as proof. Review all added loop edges, fenced counter reservations, retry eligibility checks and human rejection paths adversarially. Inspect preservation of existing protected-input/import/fencing tests and issue-work opt-in isolation from node/PR/fork behavior. Independently inspect every round-0 path, persisted key/reset point, explicit implement override and default tester-resume fenced validation write.

Reuse applicable passing developer results at the same relevant source revision. Run missing targeted cases or repeat checks only after relevant source changes, observed failures, or an unresolved coverage concern. Add a focused failing regression if a boundary is untested. Keep changed-package format/static diagnostics available. Record acceptance evidence and any remaining gap in VALIDATION.md; tester PASS never substitutes for trusted validation.

## Coordinator-owned validation and PR review

The coordinator runs the complete approved-base required policy once after agent roles finish; `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml` is a reference, not a per-role checklist. The developer owns `make check` for criterion 6 and records it in IMPLEMENTATION.md; the tester reuses an applicable passing result under the rules above. The compiled policy does not itself run make check; its changelog package tests do not replace changelog-check or the race suite. Preserve claim-bound validation on the final candidate; agent observations are advisory and cannot authorize publication. Investigate failures and repeat only affected verification after changes or unresolved concerns.

PR review checklist: maintainers may exercise one live GitHub run and a configured real harness, checking stage continuity, gate notifications, selected-context guidance and separate explicit submit. These external checks do not block sandbox implementation or replace local/fake-GitHub acceptance coverage. No automatic submit or merge is part of this WorkUnit.
